title: Passive Voice Quiz 2
description: Add being for the continuous tenses and been for the perfect tenses.
topic: Continuous and perfect tenses in the passive
instructions: Passive Voice: Continuous and perfect tenses in the passive.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'They are repairing the road'?
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: am / is / are being + past participle. Watch out: being, not been, belongs to the continuous.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'Someone has taken my bag'?
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have / has + been + past participle. Watch out: been is used with the perfect, and being with the continuous.

questions.question: The room {{1}} (clean) when I arrived. Use the past continuous.
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was / were + being + past participle. Watch out: the room is singular, so the helper is was.

questions.question: By Friday the work {{1}} (finish) and the workers {{2}} (pay). Use the future perfect.
questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle. Watch out: the participle of pay is paid, not payed.

questions.question: 'The film has being cancelled' is correct.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive is has been cancelled. Watch out: being belongs to the continuous tenses only.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The work will be finished been by Friday.
The work will have being finished by Friday.
The work has will been finished by Friday.
The work will have been finished by Friday.
questions.explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + participle. Watch out: the helpers keep their order, will then have then been.

questions.question: Choose the missing word: being or been.

rows.given: The cakes were ___ baked when we came.

questions.explanation: The continuous passive uses being, and the perfect passive uses been. Watch out: a time clue such as when we came shows an action in progress.

questions.question: Match each tense with its passive formula.
right: am / is / are being + past participle
questions.explanation: Continuous tenses add being, and perfect tenses add been. Watch out: have / has and had are the helpers of the perfect, not of the continuous.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The subject, then is, then being, then the participle. Watch out: being goes between is and painted.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: A new bridge was being built.
questions.explanation: Correct passives have the right form of be, then being or been where needed. Watch out: is being painting and has be finished use the wrong form after be or have.

questions.question: Which active sentence matches 'The cars were being washed'?
questions.explanation: Were being washed is the past continuous passive, so the active verb is was washing. Watch out: had washed would give the past perfect passive.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: The window has broken by the boys.
accepted: The window has been broken by the boys.
The window has been broken by the boys
The window was broken by the boys.
The window was broken by the boys
questions.explanation: A passive with by needs been and a participle: has been broken, or the past simple was broken. Watch out: has broken is active, so it cannot take by the boys.
